extracted.intended_audience: national trademark Offices / Office of origin officials filing Madrid Protocol notifications
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions for Offices of origin on completing Model Form 9A to notify the International Bureau that an international registration ceases to be protected (in whole or in part) because of a final decision affecting the basic mark.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of MF9A (when to use)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use this form to notify the International Bureau that the international registration will no longer be protected, in whole or in part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form is specifically for notifying loss of protection of the international registration; it is not a general communication form. Use MF9A only where the international registration ceases to be protected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible grounds for notification
rubrics_metrics.description: The international registration ceases to be protected because the basic application has been rejected or has been withdrawn; or the basic registration is canceled, renounced, revoked, invalidated or has lapsed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List the applicable ground(s) (rejected, withdrawn, canceled, renounced, revoked, invalidated, lapsed) on the form. The wording in the form matches these explicit grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality and five-year timing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision must be final and must have been issued within a period of five years from the date of the international registration, or must result from an action commenced within that five-year period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only notify the International Bureau using MF9A if the decision is final and falls within the five-year limit (or stems from proceedings begun within that period). If the decision is not final or outside the time limit, MF9A should not be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to request cancellation under Article 6(4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the basic application/registration decision meets the conditions above, the Office must request the cancellation of the international registration in accordance with Article 6(4) of the Madrid Protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filing MF9A in these circumstances, explicitly request cancellation of the international registration and cite Article 6(4) as the legal basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use after preliminary notification (MF9B)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of origin should use MF9A when it previously sent a preliminary notification under Rule 22(1)(b) using MF9B and now wishes to notify the International Bureau that the decision has become final and has resulted in rejection, withdrawal, cancellation, renunciation, revocation, invalidation or lapse of the basic mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MF9A serves as the follow-up/final notice after MF9B. Indicate that MF9B was previously sent if applicable and provide the final decision details.

rubrics_metrics.name: State whether cancellation is total or partial
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office must state whether the cancellation of the international registration is total or partial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose and indicate clearly between total cancellation (entire international registration) or partial cancellation (only some goods/services or classes).

rubrics_metrics.name: If partial, clearly indicate goods/services affected or not affected
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of partial cancellation, the Office must provide a clear indication of the goods and services that are affected or those that are NOT affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify affected items precisely. If all goods or all services in a given class are concerned, the indication should read: "all goods (or all services) in class X". Use clear class-based phrasing to avoid ambiguity.
